questions.explain: ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly in the connection string makes the AG listener redirect the connection to a readable secondary instead of the primary, offloading read load without any proxy tier.
options: The AG listener ignores the setting and routes every connection to the primary
The AG listener redirects the connection to a readable secondary automatically
The TCP load balancer parses the SQL text to decide the target
WSFC quorum votes on the intent and assigns the connection to the oldest replica
questions.q: What does ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly in a connection string do when connecting through an Availability Group listener?

questions.explain: The parenthesized group ('SQLNode2','SQLNode3') is a load-balanced set that shares ReadOnly connections equally, while SQLNode4 (outside the parens) is the fallback when both are unavailable.
options: ReadOnly connections are distributed equally between SQLNode2 and SQLNode3; SQLNode4 is the fallback
SQLNode2 gets all reads, SQLNode3 is a hot spare, and SQLNode4 is used only on Tuesdays
All three secondaries receive writes in round-robin order
The list is alphabetical, so SQLNode2 is always preferred and the rest are ignored
questions.q: In SQL Server 2016+, what does the read-only routing list (('SQLNode2', 'SQLNode3'), 'SQLNode4') mean when LOAD_BALANCE is used?

questions.explain: The PRIMARY_ROLE routing list is per-primary, so it must be repeated on every replica that can become primary — otherwise a failover silently drops read-only routing until someone reconfigures it.
options: The secondary's redo queue must be empty before any routing list takes effect
Routing lists only work with synchronous commit replicas in the same subnet
The TCP load balancer in front of the listener rewrites the routing list on every failover
The routing list must be repeated on every replica that can become primary, or failover silently drops read-only routing
questions.q: What is the chapter's operational gotcha about read-only routing lists after an AG failover?

questions.explain: A role-aware probe (e.g., sys.fn_hadr_is_primary_replica) every couple of seconds, combined with rise/fall thresholds, prevents flapping from transient network hiccups and keeps traffic off failed nodes.
options: A heavyweight reporting query once per hour, so probes never disturb the workload
A DNS lookup of the listener name with a 24-hour TTL to keep connections sticky
A lightweight T-SQL probe (e.g., SELECT 1 or sys.fn_hadr_is_primary_replica) with rise/fall thresholds
A manual ping from a DBA's laptop whenever the application reports slowness
questions.q: How should a TCP load balancer sitting in front of the AG listener health-check the SQL Server nodes?

questions.explain: If a secondary is running a long SELECT when the primary needs to truncate version store entries, cleanup is delayed — heavy reporting on secondaries can cause version store growth on the primary, so monitor redo_queue_size and version store usage.
options: Reads on secondaries are instant and have no effect on the primary, by design
Heavy reporting queries on secondaries can delay version store cleanup and cause version store growth on the primary
Secondaries automatically pause redo whenever a reporting query runs longer than 5 minutes
Version store growth is impossible on an AG because redo is synchronous
questions.q: Why should DBAs monitor version store usage when running long reporting queries against readable secondaries?
